clue.text: What one learns at charm school?

definitions.meaning: the lessons such a school of magic would give are incantations
really a finishing school for manners, but read literally it is a school teaching magical charms

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a deportment academy actually teaches its pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: A charm school teaches poise and etiquette; take charm as a magic charm and the curriculum becomes magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Charms are magical incantations, so a school of charms would teach its pupils incantations of that kind.

clue.text: New parent meets friend of one's father

definitions.note: an adverbial sense: related through or in the manner of one's father

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters of parent are formed afresh

parts.note: taken as written
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A new parent bonds with an old friend of the family's father.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes kinship traced on the father's side or behaviour typical of a father.

clue.text: Desperately tried to get in SAS with catastrophic result

indicators.note: the letters SAS get in among the rearranged letters, so they sit inside them
done desperately, the letters of tried are thrown about wildly into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frantically tried to join the SAS, and it ended badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is Britain's Special Air Service, an elite army regiment notoriously hard to join.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe or calamity is exactly a terrible outcome of this kind.

clue.text: Get ready on way to see band

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it, so the word for ready follows the road

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: An instruction to prepare yourself on the road to a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: Band looks like a musical group, but here it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour or material on a surface.

clue.text: Place in the middle in Kent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put something between two others
second meaning: a place, a town in the county of Kent

explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; the town of that name gave the snack its title through an Earl.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to squeeze between two things, and it is also the name of a historic Kentish town.

clue.text: Impressive-sounding reason to exchange books

indicators.note: the letters of reason exchange places with each other, giving a new order

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding excuse for swapping library books.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant voice or phrase is deep, ringing and so carries an impressive tone.

clue.text: I'm so fancy in outrageous lace underwear

indicators.note: the rearranged I'm so letters sit within the other group
outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of lace are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fancy suggests something elaborate and contrived, so the letters of I'm so are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admiring themselves in daring lacy lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's loose sleeveless undergarment for the upper body.

clue.text: Due to ring Wednesday

parts.note: the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Something is due because of a phone call on Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: Due to looks like the phrase meaning because of; due alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is due is still outstanding, owing to the lender.

clue.text: Scoffs at during point-to-point

indicators.note: the word at comes during the span between the two points, so inside them

parts.note: two compass points, east and south, one to the other
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at things while watching a point-to-point race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it is just two compass points. Scoffs means devours, not mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is informal for gobbling food greedily, which is what one does when one devours.

clue.text: Get close to home with the French

parts.note: a bird's nest is its home
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Settling in at home with French company.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle up or press cosily against someone.

clue.text: Declining years, not without love

parts.note: a decade is a span of ten years

indicators.note: the word not is taken without, so minus, the letter for love

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about one's later years, and they are not without romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes a society in moral or cultural decline and decay.

clue.text: Fashionable royal connection

definitions.meaning: points to dress and style, the knot being a smart way to tie a necktie
reads as a link to the royal family, whose house name it bears; connection is also a literal tie

explanation.surface: A trendy link to the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor is the British royal family's house name; the knot is a wide, symmetrical necktie knot named after the Duke of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a style of tying a necktie, a stylish fastening with a royal name attached.

clue.text: Newspaper article on call to identify chief troublemaker

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the call comes on top of the article

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
a leader is a newspaper's editorial column

explanation.surface: A paper's editorial urges readers to phone in and name the culprit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringleader is the person heading a gang or a group making mischief.

clue.text: Solid but stupid collection of objects

parts.note: thick is informal for dim-witted
a set is a group of things belonging together

explanation.surface: A dense but dim assortment of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickset person is heavily built and stocky, solid in frame.

clue.text: Starts to rudely interrupt Pinter play obsessed with sex

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: the opening letters break into the other letters, so they go inside
the letters of Pinter are played with, put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written: Harold Pinter's surname
the opening letters of the word rudely, its start

explanation.surface: Hecklers rudely disrupt a Harold Pinter play with a sexual theme.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinter was an English playwright, so play looks like a noun for a stage work; here it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an excessive or unhealthy interest in sexual matters.

clue.text: Turn right out of entrance for the restaurant

indicators.note: the remaining letters are turned around into a new order
right is taken out of the word entrance, removing it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions: turn right as you leave the entrance to reach the dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn right reads as a direction; Turn is the rearranging signal and right only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria or dining hall in a workplace, school or barracks.

clue.text: Accepts tokens of affection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, welcomes or takes up an idea
second meaning: a plural noun, hugs

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue suggests someone receiving love tokens; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for welcoming an idea and a plural noun for hugs.

clue.text: An unstable animal?

definitions.meaning: something unsteady that staggers or sways suddenly
the answer is also a dog breed, a crossbred greyhound type

explanation.walkthrough: The breed name sounds like one who staggers, so a tottering creature is a punning description of the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, often greyhound and collie, so it is a kind of hound.

clue.text: Middling sort of performer

definitions.meaning: looks like mediocre, but means one dealing with the middle of the body
the entertainer in question moves the midriff

explanation.walkthrough: Middling usually means average; here it means working with the midriff.
explanation.definitionFit: This dancer's art centres on rhythmic movements of the abdomen, the body's midsection.

clue.text: Made off without street map when in a state of shock

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters sit outside the map
off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of Made are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an A to Z is a London street atlas

explanation.surface: Someone fled without their street map and was left reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, not lacking. The A-Z is the classic British street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amazed is astonished or stunned by surprise.

clue.text: Exploited by American journalist

parts.note: ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone was taken advantage of by an American reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used means being taken advantage of by somebody for their own ends.

clue.text: Simple activity holds a strong appeal

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within them, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An easy pastime has wide attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Appeal looks like attractiveness; here it means an earnest request.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an urgent, emotional request, such as for mercy.

clue.text: Fruit and nut salsa blend

indicators.note: blending mixes things up, so the letters of nut salsa are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for a dip mixing fruit, nuts and salsa.
explanation.definitionFit: These are dried seedless grapes, a common dried produce in baking.

clue.text: Problem for husband when son left halfway through

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he arrived
the first half of the word left

explanation.surface: Trouble for a husband when his son walked out midway.
explanation.walkthrough: Halfway through reads as the timing of the son's departure; halfway applies to the word left itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is an annoying bother or difficulty.

clue.text: Rejected help when unusually beset by illness

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the word for help is turned backwards

parts.note: aid is help or assistance

indicators.note: the letters of beset are placed in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turned down assistance when oddly troubled by sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a chronic disease in which the body cannot regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: How to clean the carpet and go away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an instruction to whack the rug to drive out dust
second meaning: a slang command to clear off

explanation.walkthrough: Carpets were once cleaned by hanging them out and beating them; the same phrase is slang for scram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rude order to leave and, literally, the way to dust a rug by beating.
